text.arabic_uthmani: لَّوْلَا جَآءُو عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ ۚ فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُوا۟ بِٱلشُّهَدَآءِ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلْكَٰذِبُونَ

words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) makes the ayah begin as a procedural rebuke: why was the required proof not produced? It is not a counterfactual condition or a simple negation; it opens the demand beat that will be answered by the negated failure and the final liar-verdict. Its recurrence after 24:12 keeps two obligations side by side: believers should have judged the report rightly, and the accusers should have produced witnesses.

topics.headline: reproachful proof demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens with a rebuke for missing proof, not with a neutral condition or simple negation.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) as a reproachful particle governing the following production clause.

topics.headline: fused particle form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question-like opening is a fixed procedural rebuke, not a transparent sequence of separate particles.
topics.reason: The fixed-particle analysis keeps {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) from being parsed as free conditional plus ordinary negation.

topics.headline: demand-to-verdict frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one opening particle launches the ayah's logic: demand, confirmed failure, then verdict.
topics.reason: The clause evidence confirms that {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) opens the demand beat on which the later failure and verdict depend.

topics.headline: paired reproach with 24:12
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 24:12 and 24:13 share a reproach opening, pairing moral reception of the report with legal production of proof.
topics.reason: The concrete 24:12 comparison survives because both ayahs open with the same reproach particle while assigning different obligations.

words.gloss_range: bring/produce witnesses in a reproach frame; not mere arrival
words.root_gloss_range: root range of coming and arrival, locally narrowed by bi-governed evidence production
words.prose: {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) carries the missed action demanded by the opening particle: the accusers themselves should have brought proof, not caused others to appear. The plural verb keeps that group responsible, and the following {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) phrase narrows the coming-root into evidentiary production, not simple arrival. Its pairing with {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) makes the same required act reappear as the act they failed to do, while 24:11 sharpens the reversal: the report was brought, but witnesses were not. The hamza sounds in {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}), and {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) make demand, failure, and verdict audible as distinct stops.

topics.headline: perfect verb under reproach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb marks an action that should already have happened: proof-production was expected and absent.
topics.reason: The perfect verb after {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) supports a reproach over a missed required action.

topics.headline: plural subject bears responsibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accuser group remains grammatically present even before it is named again by the demonstrative.
topics.reason: The 3mp ending and pro-drop evidence keep the responsible group encoded in {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}).

topics.headline: motion verb becomes evidence production
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that proof must be brought forward into the legal scene, while the local prepositional frame selects production rather than mere arrival.
topics.reason: The root's coming image survives as brought-forward evidence, but the local {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) frame narrows the sense to producing witnesses.

topics.headline: uncausative Form I keeps agency on accusers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusers themselves are the ones required to produce the evidence, not to cause someone else to appear.
topics.reason: The Form I verb and its local complements keep agency with the plural subject of {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}).

topics.headline: near-synonym production pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demanded act and the failed act are tied by near-synonym bring verbs rather than flat repetition.
topics.reason: {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) and {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) form a local demand/failure pair.

topics.headline: slander brought, witnesses not brought
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reversal from a report that was brought in 24:11 to witnesses that were not brought in 24:13.
topics.reason: The 24:11 and 24:13 comparison is concrete and locally relevant: what circulated as report is forced into proof-production.

topics.headline: hamza stops articulate the argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demand, failure, and verdict are made audible as distinct steps by repeated glottal interruptions.
topics.reason: The hamza in {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}), and {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) supports the sound-texture claim without changing the lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: forensic target marker: concerning it or against him
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) gives the proof demand a target. It is governed by {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) and comes before the witness instrument, so the ayah first marks what the testimony must address. The suffix keeps a useful legal ambiguity: the proof may concern the slandered report carried from 24:12 or be testimony against the accused party, but the local frame is forensic rather than spatial.

topics.headline: target complement of the proof verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah first fixes what the testimony must address, then names the witness instrument.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) a complement of {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), placed before the witness phrase.

topics.headline: pronoun keeps two legal routings live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the suffix can route testimony either to the slander/report or against the accused party, preserving the forensic target without over-specifying it.
topics.reason: The guardrails mark the pronoun target as discourse-linked, so both concerning-it and against-him routings remain legally live.

topics.headline: upon-ness becomes forensic targeting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition places the claim under evidentiary burden, while local syntax blocks a physical upon-reading.
topics.reason: The spatial value of {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) is narrowed by the testimony frame to forensic targeting.

topics.headline: suffix binds the target into the preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the heard report from 24:12 is carried forward as the object that now demands proof.
topics.reason: The preposition-plus-suffix form and boundary evidence support continuity from the prior report into this evidentiary target.

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) is structurally essential: it turns {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) from simple coming into bringing evidence. It governs the four-witness phrase, so the witnesses are both brought with the accusers and function as the means of verification. As a short bound proclitic, it leans into the number phrase rather than standing as an afterthought. Its later repetition before the definite witness phrase makes the ayah's evidentiary arc easy to track.

topics.headline: preposition supplies evidence object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this small preposition is what turns coming into producing the four witnesses.
topics.reason: The first {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) governs the number phrase and supplies the proof object of {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}).

topics.headline: accompaniment and instrument together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witnesses are both the people the accusers must come with and the means by which the claim could be verified.
topics.reason: The local legal frame allows both accompaniment and instrumentality for {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}).

topics.headline: bound particle ties number to verb phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the short bound form makes the evidence phrase lean into the verb rather than stand as an afterthought.
topics.reason: The proclitic shape of {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) visibly and audibly attaches the witness number to the production frame.

topics.headline: first slot in repeated evidence arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this first proof slot will be repeated later with the definite witnesses, creating demand then failure.
topics.reason: The first {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) introduces the indefinite requirement that word 11 reprises before the definite witness noun.

words.gloss_range: cardinal four as exact evidentiary threshold
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes four, fourth, quartering, fourfold making, and other branches; locally the cardinal count is active
words.prose: {{ar:أَرْبَعَةِ}} ({{tr:arbaʿati}}) fixes the demand as exactly four witnesses. The genitive cardinal is bound to the counted witness noun, and its feminine shape is the normal number-gender polarity for a masculine counted plural, not semantic feminization. Root-family fourfold imagery can color the threshold as complete support, but the local form selects the cardinal count, not an ordinal, fraction, or unrelated branch. The wording applies the Surah 24 witness standard seen in 24:4 and 24:6, and the short number sets up the heavier witness word as the cadence landing point.

topics.headline: genitive cardinal governs witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the number is grammatically locked to the witness noun, with Arabic number-gender polarity marking exact enumeration.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support {{ar:أَرْبَعَةِ}} ({{tr:arbaʿati}}) as the governed cardinal in the four-witness construction.

topics.headline: four as fixed evidentiary threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah demands a fixed threshold, not a vague plurality or approximate support.
topics.reason: The indefinite demand phrase sets a category threshold before the later definite reprise measures failure against it.

topics.headline: fourfold stability image under exact count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a complete four-part proof frame, while local form keeps the active sense as the cardinal number itself.
topics.reason: V4 permits four/fourfold branches, but the local cardinal form narrows the payoff to exact count rather than broad quartering or settlement imagery.

topics.headline: cardinal not ordinal or fraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form names four persons as a threshold, not rank, sequence, or share.
topics.reason: The local cardinal form blocks ordinal and fractional derivatives as active local senses.

topics.headline: Surah 24 four-witness standard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 24:13 applies an already recognizable Quranic and Surah 24 witness threshold, especially 24:4 and 24:6.
topics.reason: The supplied references connect {{ar:أَرْبَعَةِ}} ({{tr:arbaʿati}}) with the witness requirement in 24:4, 24:6, and related legal material.

topics.headline: number phrase lands on witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the short number sets up the heavier witness word as the audible landing point of the demand.
topics.reason: The cadence claim is locally tied to the number-plus-witness phrase and does not alter the lexical parse.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural witnesses required as legal attestors
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes presence, seeing, testimony, attestation, martyrdom, signs, and other branches; local sense is courtroom witnesshood
words.prose: {{ar:شُهَدَاءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}) completes the four-witness requirement. Its indefinite form sets a category of valid attestors, while the root's presence-and-testimony range makes the demand stronger than hearsay. The ayah does not ask others to testify; it rebukes the accusers for failing to produce the witnesses themselves. The broader martyr use belongs to the same root family, but the local number phrase and legal production verb select courtroom witnesses. Its later definite reprise turns this demanded category into the known standard they failed to meet, linking witnesshood to divine adjudication and the final falsehood label. The Surah 24 legal network at 24:4, 24:6, and 24:8 remains in view, and the final hamza in both witness plurals makes the demand and reprise audibly pointed.

topics.headline: indefinite demanded witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first witness phrase sets a required category before any particular set is treated as known.
topics.reason: The article-less form of {{ar:شُهَدَاءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}) contrasts with the definite reprise at word 12.

topics.headline: counted noun completes the four
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah requires four witnesses specifically, not four items or supports in general.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:شُهَدَاءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}) the counted complement of {{ar:أَرْبَعَةِ}} ({{tr:arbaʿati}}).

topics.headline: presence-based attestors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the required witnesses are presence-based attestors, not transmitters of hearsay.
topics.reason: The accepted witness/testimony branches fit the local legal frame for {{ar:شُهَدَاءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}).

topics.headline: unstated request form sharpens burden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not ask others to testify; it rebukes the accusers for failing to produce the witnesses themselves.
topics.reason: The Form X request image remains comparative background, while the local wording uses {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) to place production burden on the accusers.

topics.headline: courtroom witness over martyr sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shared witness/martyr root family, while the legal number phrase selects courtroom attestors here.
topics.reason: The martyr branch is valid root-family background, but the four-witness legal frame narrows {{ar:شُهَدَاءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}) to attesting witnesses.

topics.headline: broken plural forms a legal class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural gathers individual attestors into the required witness body while preserving plurality.
topics.reason: The broken plural form supports the class-of-witness-bearers claim.

topics.headline: witnesses mediate divine verdict and falsehood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that witnesshood is the hinge between divine adjudication and the final falsehood label.
topics.reason: The supplied co-occurrence fields are locally realized by witnesses, divine judgment, and the liar predicate in the same ayah.

topics.headline: demand becomes definite failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the legal movement from a required witness category to the specific required witnesses not produced.
topics.reason: The repeated witness noun with a definiteness shift structures the demand/failure hinge.

topics.headline: Surah 24 testimony network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this witness term externalizes the report into public adjudication within Surah 24's legal testimony material.
topics.reason: The supplied references to 24:4, 24:6, and 24:8 keep the Surah 24 legal network concrete.

topics.headline: hamza lands on witness term
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both witness plurals close with a pointed sound, making demand and failed reprise audible.
topics.reason: The sound claim is anchored in the two local witness plurals.

words.gloss_range: causal-sequential hinge into the failure clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) opens the failure clause as a causal hinge: since the demanded witnesses were not produced, the verdict can follow. Bound to {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}), it makes the shift from demand to established failure immediate, and it anticipates the second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) that will introduce the consequence. The two short {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) onsets make the ayah's logical hinges audible: failure-ground, then verdict.

topics.headline: first connective makes failure causal ground
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the next clause is not mere continuation; non-production becomes the reason the verdict can follow.
topics.reason: QAC and clause-link evidence support the first {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) as sequence with causal force.

topics.headline: bound to the failure-time particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an immediate pivot from the demand into assessed failure, with no loose sentence break.
topics.reason: The surface fusion with {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) makes the hinge compact.

topics.headline: first half of paired connective cascade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's two audible hinges: one opens the failure ground, the other releases the verdict.
topics.reason: Words 7 and 13 form the repeated connective architecture of the ayah.

words.prose: {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) makes the failure clause a ground for judgment: since or when they did not bring the witnesses. It points to a realized condition rather than a hypothetical future one, so the ayah establishes non-production before moving to the verdict. As a fixed particle, it anchors the whole negated clause before the verdict is released. Across 24:12 and 24:13, the temporal framing shifts from hearing the report to adjudicating the missing proof.

topics.headline: since/when grounds verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict rests on an established failure, not just on the time at which something happened.
topics.reason: The temporal-causal clause evidence supports {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) as the ground for the verdict.

topics.headline: settled condition rather than future hypothesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the non-production of witnesses is treated as settled fact before the liar label is pronounced.
topics.reason: The distinction from future-hypothetical particles supports a realized-condition reading for {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}).

topics.headline: indeclinable anchor for negated clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the compact particle anchors the whole negated clause before the verdict is released.
topics.reason: The fixed particle form supports its clause-anchoring role without adding verbal agreement.

topics.headline: from hearing moment to proof failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the temporal framing from 24:12 is reused for a new procedural scene: report reception becomes proof failure.
topics.reason: The 24:12 to 24:13 shift is concrete and local to the two adjacent ayahs.

words.gloss_range: jussive negation of the required witness-production
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) is the ayah's explicit negation hinge. It governs {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) into a past-negated jussive and denies the production of the definite witnesses as a completed non-event, with negation visibly outside the verb while controlling its mood. The verdict depends on categorical noncompliance, not ambiguous shortage: the opening asks why proof was not brought, and {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) confirms that it was not.

topics.headline: jussive past negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure is grammatically presented as a completed non-event: they did not bring the witnesses.
topics.reason: QAC confirms {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) governs the imperfect verb into jussive past negation.

topics.headline: particle controls form and polarity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that negation remains visibly outside the verb while controlling its mood, making the failed action easy to parse.
topics.reason: The separate particle form and jussive governance both survive locally.

topics.headline: categorical evidentiary noncompliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the issue is not uncertainty or partial support; the required threshold was not met.
topics.reason: The negation scopes over bringing the definite witnesses, so the legal noncompliance is categorical.

topics.headline: negation bridges demand and verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening 'why not' is answered by the explicit 'they did not,' which makes the verdict follow.
topics.reason: The clause structure confirms {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) as the hinge between demand and verdict.

words.root_gloss_range: root range of coming, arriving, bringing, and related giving branches; locally Form I with bi selects purposeful presentation
words.prose: {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) names the action that did not happen. After {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}), the imperfect becomes a past-negated jussive, and with {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) it means bringing or presenting the witnesses, not merely arriving; the directed-arrival image survives as proof failing to reach the adjudicating space. The Form I verb keeps the action in arrival/presentation, not Form IV giving. The verb answers {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) with near-synonym variation, recalls the 24:4 witness-production requirement as an unmet standard, and sits between the witness object and the liar verdict. Its internal hamza audibly interrupts the negated act.

topics.headline: bi-governed production of witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failed act is purposeful presentation of proof, not merely coming somewhere.
topics.reason: The {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) complement locally converts {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) into bringing/presenting witnesses.

topics.headline: jussive imperfect records negated event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical shift from expected past production to negated compliance.
topics.reason: The imperfect jussive after {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) carries past negation.

topics.headline: missing proof as failed arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the image of proof failing to arrive into the adjudicating space, while local syntax selects evidentiary production.
topics.reason: The directed-arrival image survives as a concrete payoff, but the {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) frame narrows the local sense.

topics.headline: same plural group remains under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same accuser group is responsible in both the demand and the failure clause.
topics.reason: The 3mp ending in {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) matches {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) and keeps the responsible group constant.

topics.headline: arrival/presentation not bestowal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the active frame is presentation of witnesses, while the giving/granting branch is excluded by the local Form I parse.
topics.reason: The local form is Form I, so Form IV giving is not the active sense here.

topics.headline: 24:4 requirement becomes failed in 24:13
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same witness-production structure from 24:4 is now the structure they failed to satisfy.
topics.reason: The concrete 24:4 comparison supports the procedural recurrence of the witness-production frame.

topics.headline: failed production triggers falsehood verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this verb is the compliance test between witnesses and the liar label.
topics.reason: The local sequence places {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) between the witness object and the final predicate.

topics.headline: answers opening verb with variation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices continuity of the required act through lexical variation: what should have been brought is what was not brought.
topics.reason: The near-synonym pair {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) and {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) supports the demand/failure echo.

topics.headline: glottal stop marks the failed action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible interruption at the very verb that names the missing act.
topics.reason: The sound claim is locally anchored in the hamza of {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) inside the negated phrase.

words.gloss_range: bound preposition introducing the definite missing witnesses
words.prose: The second {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) mirrors the first proof preposition. It makes {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}) mean bring the witnesses and now binds to a definite noun, so the ayah measures failure against the already stated standard. The witnesses are missing both as companions brought with the accusers and as the proof-channel for verification. The compact preposition-plus-definite phrase lets the reader compare demanded proof with unproduced proof in the same grammatical slot.

topics.headline: second preposition frames missing object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same preposition again turns coming into bringing, now for the witnesses not produced.
topics.reason: The second {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) governs the definite witness noun as object frame for {{ar:يَأْتُوا}} ({{tr:yaʾtū}}).

topics.headline: definite witnesses as accompaniment and proof-channel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the missing witnesses are both absent companions and the absent means of verification.
topics.reason: The legal frame keeps accompaniment and instrumentality together for the second {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}).

topics.headline: bound preposition with definite witness noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second evidence phrase is more specific and compact because it binds to the definite witness noun.
topics.reason: The bound preposition plus article-bearing noun supports the compact definite-evidence phrase.

topics.headline: parallel slot tracks demand and failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated prepositional slot compares the first demanded witness phrase with the second failed witness phrase.
topics.reason: The two {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) slots structure the evidentiary arc from indefinite demand to definite failure.

words.gloss_range: the already required witnesses, concrete attesting persons
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes presence, seeing, testimony, attestation, martyrdom, signs, and other branches; local sense is definite courtroom witnesses
words.prose: {{ar:الشُّهَدَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-shuhadāʾi}}) is the definite reprise of the earlier witness category. The article makes the standard anaphoric: these are the witnesses already demanded. Governed by the second {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}), the noun remains concrete and plural, so the failure is not abstract lack of testimony but non-production of the required presence-based attestors. Its definiteness makes the standard known while the broken plural keeps multiple witnesses in view, and the compact {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}})-plus-witness phrase turns the failure directly toward the liar predicate.

topics.headline: the already demanded witnesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the article points back to the witnesses already required, not to witnesses in general.
topics.reason: The definite form of {{ar:الشُّهَدَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-shuhadāʾi}}) is anaphoric after the earlier indefinite {{ar:شُهَدَاءَ}} ({{tr:shuhadāʾa}}).

topics.headline: genitive object of second preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the definite witnesses are the missing brought object of the negated verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:الشُّهَدَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-shuhadāʾi}}) governed by the second {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}).

topics.headline: attestors not abstract testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure concerns concrete presence-based witnesses, not an abstract idea of testimony.
topics.reason: The definite broken plural and witness branch support concrete attesting persons.

topics.headline: known plural witness body
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that definiteness makes the standard known while the broken plural keeps multiple attestors in view.
topics.reason: The morphology preserves plural witnesshood after the article makes the category definite.

topics.headline: failed witnesses trigger liar predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the liar verdict follows failure to produce the specified presence-based witnesses, not a general lack of support.
topics.reason: The local sequence connects non-production of {{ar:الشُّهَدَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-shuhadāʾi}}) directly to the final predicate.

topics.headline: definite reprise measures failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar of legal procedure: first state the standard, then measure noncompliance against that standard.
topics.reason: The intra-ayah echo from indefinite to definite witness noun carries the procedural arc.

topics.headline: compact governed witness phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the short preposition and definite witness noun are heard as one compact evidentiary phrase.
topics.reason: The recitation/surface claim is tied to {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi-}}) plus {{ar:الشُّهَدَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-shuhadāʾi}}).

words.gloss_range: consequential hinge into the verdict clause
words.prose: The second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) releases the verdict from the established failure. It binds directly to {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}), so the condemned group appears as the consequence of not bringing the witnesses. Together with the earlier {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}), it gives the ayah a ground-to-verdict cascade, with two short onsets audibly bracketing failure and consequence.

topics.headline: consequential verdict particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the liar statement is an inference from failed proof, not a detached insult.
topics.reason: The second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) introduces the result clause after the established failure.

topics.headline: consequence fused to demonstrative subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condemned group appears as the immediate result of the failed witness clause.
topics.reason: The bound form attaches the connective directly to {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}).

topics.headline: second half of double-fa cascade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the two-step logic: the first connective grounds failure, the second releases judgment.
topics.reason: The paired connective architecture is confirmed by the clause sequence c2 to c3.

words.gloss_range: distant demonstrative subject identifying the accusers
words.prose: {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) points to the accusers as the subject of the verdict clause. Its distance is evaluative as well as deictic: those people, held away from the addressee's moral space, are now placed under the predicate. The nominal structure makes the final statement an identity verdict rather than a report of one event. After 24:12's direct address to the community, this third-person demonstrative shifts the scene to the distanced accusers.

topics.headline: demonstrative identifies accusers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final label is aimed at the witnessless accusers, not at an undefined class of people.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence points {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) back to the slander-bearing accusers who failed to bring witnesses.

topics.headline: subject of nominal verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict is an identity statement, not a passing event.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:أُولَئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) the subject of the nominal clause whose predicate is {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}).

topics.headline: far demonstrative creates distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar holds the accusers at evaluative distance before naming their falsehood.
topics.reason: The far-deictic form supports moral/evaluative distancing in this verdict context.

topics.headline: from addressed community to condemned those
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a discourse shift from the community's responsibility in 24:12 to the distanced accusers condemned in 24:13.
topics.reason: The 24:12 to 24:13 boundary evidence supports the shift from direct address to third-person verdict group.

words.root_gloss_range: root range includes proximity, presence, judgment/opinion, obstinacy, sidewardness, and other branches; locally the adverbial judgment frame is active
words.prose: {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) relocates the verdict into God's assessment. It governs {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) and stands between the demonstrative subject and the liar predicate, so divine evaluation intervenes before the label lands. The root's nearness image remains useful as assessment-space pressure, placing the accusers before God's assessment, but local grammar selects the adverbial judgment frame, not physical proximity or the rare obstinacy adjective. The Surah 24 recurrence at 24:15 and 24:39 keeps this assessment-location marker in the surah's wider evaluative field.

topics.headline: adverbial frame controls assessment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict is located within an assessment frame, so the decisive perspective is God's judgment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) as the adverbial frame governing the divine name and modifying the verdict.

topics.headline: proximity becomes judgment frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusers are placed before God's assessment, while local syntax selects evaluative judgment rather than physical nearness or possession.
topics.reason: The proximity/presence branch survives as assessment-space pressure, but the predicate {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) narrows {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) to God's judgment.

topics.headline: adverb not obstinacy adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that any resistance coloring remains background; the active local form is the common adverbial judgment marker.
topics.reason: V4 separates adjectival obstinacy branches from the local adverbial {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) form.

topics.headline: strong divine judgment pairing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase with God's name becomes the ayah's syntactic and semantic pivot before the liar predicate lands.
topics.reason: The {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) plus {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) pairing governs the divine evaluator in the verdict.

topics.headline: divine assessment inserted before predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine assessment stands between the demonstrative subject and the final liar predicate.
topics.reason: Word order places {{ar:عِنْدَ اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ʿinda Allāhi}}) before {{ar:هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:humu al-kādhibūna}}).

topics.headline: from community cognition to divine adjudication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from human hearing and evaluation in 24:12 to God's judgment frame in 24:13, with related Surah 24 uses at 24:15 and 24:39.
topics.reason: The supplied references keep the Surah 24 assessment-location motif concrete.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as genitive evaluator in the verdict frame
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with documented derivational density; local role is the unique divine evaluator governed by the assessment frame
words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) as the divine assessment frame. The proper name makes the verdict uniquely located with God, not with a replaceable observer, and its genitive case shows that this is a governed phrase. The divine name is semantically dense in derivational discussion, but here its local role is adjudicative. Placed before the final predicate, it stands between the accusers and the label that condemns them. Same-surah coming/finding before divine reckoning is visible at 24:39, and oath falsehood language at 24:7 and 24:8 is gathered here into a direct divine-side verdict after 24:12's communal obligation.

topics.headline: proper divine name as evaluator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the liar verdict is measured by God's knowledge, not by a replaceable human observer.
topics.reason: The proper divine name {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes the judgment frame as unique evaluator.

topics.headline: genitive complement of assessment frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine name is grammatically governed inside the assessment phrase, not loosely appended to the verdict.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) in genitive after {{ar:عِنْدَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}).

topics.headline: divine-name derivation remains background
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the semantic density of the divine name, while the local role is still proper-name adjudication.
topics.reason: The documented derivational dispute can be preserved as background, but it does not override the local proper-name function of {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}).

topics.headline: failed production meets divine reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a Surah 24 pattern in which coming or finding is brought before divine reckoning, especially 24:39.
topics.reason: The concrete 24:39 comparison is relevant as a same-surah pairing, not as a replacement for the local legal frame.

topics.headline: divine name links oath and verdict falsehood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Surah 24's oath falsehood language at 24:7 and 24:8 is gathered into a direct divine-side verdict in 24:13.
topics.reason: The supplied 24:7 and 24:8 links make the oath-to-verdict movement concrete.

topics.headline: divine authority before predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that God's name structurally stands between the identified group and the predicate that condemns them.
topics.reason: Word order places {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) before {{ar:هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:humu al-kādhibūna}}).

topics.headline: from believers' obligation to God's reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the community's required response in 24:12 is measured against the divine authority that now declares the verdict.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence supports the handoff from communal obligation to divine reckoning.

words.gloss_range: separating pronoun with emphatic restrictive force
words.prose: {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) is the small word that makes the verdict snap into place. As a separating pronoun, it marks {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) as the predicate and gives the identification restrictive force: those people, they are the liars, not the accused target. The pronoun also delays the final noun with a short audible buffer, so the reversal of accusation is heard before the verdict lands. Its separation makes the predicate unmistakable.

topics.headline: separating pronoun marks predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the following definite noun is the predicate, not a mere adjective or loose apposition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence and grammar support {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) as an independent separating pronoun before the predicate.

topics.headline: they, not the accused, are liars
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the label is restrictively redirected onto the witnessless accusers, not the accused target.
topics.reason: The emphatic/restrictive force of {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) is supported by its position between subject and predicate.

topics.headline: pronoun redirects accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the accusation turning back: those who accused without witnesses become the people bearing the liar label before God.
topics.reason: The pronoun's structural insertion realizes the reversal from failed proof to liar verdict.

topics.headline: short buffer before final predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a brief audible delay before the heavy final predicate, increasing the verdict weight.
topics.reason: The sound claim is locally tied to the short pronoun before {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}).

topics.headline: grammatical separation makes verdict clear
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that clarity becomes grammar: separation identifies the predicate, restricts the label, and delays the final noun.
topics.reason: The boundary and summary rows converge on {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) as the word that makes the verdict unmistakable.

words.gloss_range: definite active participle: the liars, falsehood agents
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes falsehood, declaring false, urging formulas, failed charges, and other branches; locally Form I active participial falsehood status is selected
words.prose: {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) is the ayah's final predicate and landing point. As a definite active participle, it classifies the witnessless accusers as bearers of a falsehood status, not merely people who performed one past act, and its plural nominative ending matches the condemned group. The local form selects Form I liar/fabricator, not the Form II role of calling someone else false. After the demand and confirmed failure, the label is reached through absence of witnesses and God's judgment frame, then turns the accusation back onto its producers. The opening demand is answered by this closing verdict, while oath falsehood language at 24:7 and 24:8 becomes direct declaration here; the long ending gives the verdict a sustained close, and the boundary moves from the inverted report to the people named as liars.

topics.headline: definite classifying predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word classifies the group as the liars in this evidentiary setting, not as merely people with one described quality.
topics.reason: The definite active participle {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) is the predicate of the nominal verdict clause.

topics.headline: active participle gives falsehood status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah assigns a standing falsehood status after failed proof, not just narrating one past lie.
topics.reason: The active participle form makes {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) a status label in the nominal clause.

topics.headline: Form I liars not Form II deniers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusers are labeled active producers of falsehood, not merely people who reject or call another claim false.
topics.reason: The falsehood branch is active, while the Form II denying/accusing-of-falsehood branch is not the local form.

topics.headline: unsupported claim becomes falsehood-bearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict goes beyond procedural insufficiency: the claim-makers bear moral and epistemic falsehood.
topics.reason: The root falsehood branch and divine assessment frame support the moral-epistemic force.

topics.headline: nominative plural matches verdict group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a clear subject-predicate match: the condemned group is grammatically plural and rational.
topics.reason: The sound masculine plural nominative ending agrees with the demonstrative verdict subject.

topics.headline: falsehood reached through witnesses and God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final label is reached through two gates: absence of witnesses and God's judgment frame.
topics.reason: The local sequence contains the witness field, {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}), and {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) in one verdict movement.

topics.headline: final predicate reverses accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation's force turns back onto the accusers as the ayah's final landing point.
topics.reason: The final predicate resolves the demand/failure sequence by placing the liar label on the witnessless accusers.

topics.headline: specific failure becomes status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that failure to produce witnesses is generalized into an identity/status verdict.
topics.reason: The nominal predicate tail classifies the actors rather than narrating only a missed act.

topics.headline: opening demand and oath falsehood converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening proof demand is answered by the closing liar verdict, while nearby oath language at 24:7 and 24:8 becomes direct declaration here.
topics.reason: The concrete references 24:7, 24:8, and the opening {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) keep the ring and oath motifs grounded.

topics.headline: long ending gives verdict weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the long plural ending gives the final verdict a sustained acoustic close.
topics.reason: The -ūna ending of {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) supports the closure-weight claim.

topics.headline: from inverted report to named liars
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary handoff from naming the report as inverted falsehood to naming its producers as liars through the ayah's demand-failure-verdict logic.
topics.reason: The summary and boundary rows converge on {{ar:الْكَاذِبُونَ}} ({{tr:al-kādhibūna}}) as the ayah's landing point after the procedural sequence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired construction "they bring it against him with four witnesses / they do not bring the witnesses."
baseline_models.mechanism: An allegation that has arrived against someone must be converted into produced, observation-grounded testimony through a fixed four-person evidentiary route; nonproduction reverses the public truth-status onto the accusers.

activation_trace.role: Bringing and presenting turns the allegation's arrival into a demand for produced evidence.
The exact count fixes a public corroboration threshold.
Presence with direct observation supplies the witnesses' sensory basis.
Knowledge-bearing declaration converts observed presence into testimony.
Coming to an affair through its proper avenue makes non-arrival a failure of evidentiary method.
Contrariety to truth supplies the status produced by failure to substantiate.

changed_reading.before: The accusers should provide four witnesses; otherwise they are called liars.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an evidentiary delivery protocol: a charge must arrive as fourfold, observation-grounded testimony through the proper route, or its asserted truth-status returns against its speakers.

baseline_models.mechanism: The four are not only a tally but a load-bearing corroborative assembly: distinct observed strands are twisted together so that no single assertion carries the charge alone.

activation_trace.role: A four-force twist supplies the material image of several strands made jointly strong.
Shared lifting makes the four witnesses joint bearers of one evidentiary load.
Each strand remains anchored in witnessed presence rather than repeated report.
The assembled strands function by converging as knowledge-bearing declarations.

changed_reading.before: Four is only a numerical minimum.
changed_reading.after: Four also images a load-bearing braid: several observational strands jointly carry a charge that no solitary assertion may bear.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The emphatic clause "at God, they are the liars."
baseline_models.mechanism: The failure is located at a divine criterion of judgment, so it is not neutral missing paperwork; it assigns an accountable speech-status to those who publicly accused without the required support.

activation_trace.role: Proximity in judgment or rank locates the classification at God's criterion.
The divine name makes the governing forum explicit.
Attribution to lying supplies the status assigned to the unsupported accusers.

changed_reading.before: They are socially branded liars because they did not satisfy a procedure.
changed_reading.after: The emphatic classification is borne before God's criterion: unsupported accusatory speech itself becomes an accountable liar-status.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact rule for verbal accusation of a protected person is followed by a distinct spouse procedure: four first-person attestations are sealed by a fifth self-imprecation. This separates ordinary external corroboration from an exceptional oath-backed substitute.

activation_trace.role: The focus requires testimony that declares from knowledge.
Verbal casting identifies the initiating act as an accusation launched by speech.
Protective enclosure makes the accused person's guarded standing part of the mechanism.
The repeated rule links knowledge-bearing witnesses to both proof and the accuser's later testimonial standing.
Four reappears as the count of repeated spouse attestations rather than four external persons.
The fifth adds a self-endangering seal that distinguishes this exceptional sequence from ordinary proof.

structural_cues: 24:4 repeats the focus formula before punishment and rejection of later testimony.
24:6-9 uses four attestations plus a fifth sanction only in the spouse sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact repetition and the four-plus-fifth sequence; I infer that independent witnesses are the ordinary route while self-attestation is an exceptional substitute made costly by self-imprecation. A live alternative is that the sequence contrasts case-specific sanctions without offering a general taxonomy of evidence.

changed_reading.before: Every accusation can be established by four verbal affirmations of the same kind.
changed_reading.after: The focus names ordinary external corroboration; fourfold first-person oath testimony plus a fifth sanction is a spouse-specific substitute, so repetition and independent witnessing are not interchangeable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding sequence tracks a report from inversion, through hearing, flowing talk, reception by tongues, and onward spread without knowledge. Four observation-grounded witnesses become the gate that prevents socially mobile speech from being converted into a public fact.

activation_trace.role: Witnessed presence anchors the focus on direct observation rather than circulated speech.
Inversion supplies a report turned away from its proper truthful orientation.
Auditory reception marks the first social handoff, which is not yet witnessing.
Speech and news spreading like overflow gives rumor a fluid transmission mechanism.
Receiving and passing on speech models a relay rather than independent observation.
The explicit lack of disclosed knowledge exposes the relay's epistemic deficit.
Diffusion and circulation show the social scale reached when the relay is not stopped.

structural_cues: 24:11 begins with a group bringing the inversion; 24:12 responds at the moment of hearing.
24:15 names tongue-to-mouth transmission without knowledge, and 24:19 names desired diffusion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a staged transmission chain and the focus supplies the witness threshold; I infer that the threshold interrupts conversion of heard speech into assertable knowledge. A live alternative is that only the originating accusers, not every repeater, bear the focus clause's full legal status.

changed_reading.before: The verse only tells the original accusers to substantiate their charge.
changed_reading.after: It inserts a circuit breaker into a rumor relay: heard, received, or spreading speech remains inverted report until four observation-grounded witnesses convert it into accountable public knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly guards persons, interiors, sightlines, and sexual privacy. The extraordinary witness threshold therefore regulates public accusation without licensing intrusive observation: only multiply accountable direct sight can cross from a protected domain into public judgment.

activation_trace.role: Presence with seeing supplies the focus anchor whose access must be disciplined.
Enclosure and protection frame the accused as socially guarded rather than open to casual exposure.
Entry into an interior supplies the spatial boundary around private knowledge.
Permission makes crossing that spatial boundary an authorized act.
Restraint and lowering make vision ethically limited rather than acquisitive.
Actual eyesight clarifies the sensory channel that witnesses would have to account for.
Guarding sanctity and chastity supplies the protected value served by the high threshold.

structural_cues: 24:27-31 coordinates permission to enter, restraint of sight, and guarding private parts.
24:58-60 again regulates permission and clothing at exposed times.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies controlled entry, controlled seeing, and guarded chastity; I infer that the four-witness rule is a privacy-preserving publication threshold rather than an invitation to surveillance. A live alternative is that the privacy rules form a separate domain and only analogically illuminate accusation procedure.

changed_reading.before: Demanding four witnesses primarily maximizes exposure of a private act.
changed_reading.after: The threshold belongs to a privacy architecture: it minimizes unauthorized exposure and permits public accusation only when direct sight is extraordinarily and multiply accountable.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later testimony is carried by bodily organs and matched to performed deeds, after which truth is fully rendered and the accused are separated from what was said. This expands a witness from a mere speaker into an accountable bearer of trace.

activation_trace.role: Knowledge-bearing declaration anchors the focus's human testimonial demand.
Testimony by present bodily bearers makes witnessing inseparable from the actor's own embodied trace.
The speaking organ becomes a witness rather than an unaccountable relay.
What the hands acquired connects testimony to produced action.
The bodily foot supplies another independently located bearer of the deed.
The working limb binds witnessed speech to enacted conduct.
Truth fixed to reality names the result of the complete audit.
Separation and acquittal detach protected persons from the sayings laid on them.

structural_cues: 24:24 personifies tongues, hands, and feet as witnesses to deeds.
24:25-26 moves from full truthful recompense to acquittal from what people say.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies embodied testimony, completed truth, and separation from sayings; I infer a general contrast between trace-bearing witness and detachable speech. A live alternative is that the eschatological body scene does not prescribe the form of present legal evidence.

changed_reading.before: A witness is merely a person who gives a verbal report.
changed_reading.after: A witness is an accountable bearer whose report is tied to trace and action; external witnesses are demanded now because the divine forum ultimately makes even speaking and acting organs answer for what occurred.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later visual sequence distinguishes appearance, supposition, arrival, finding, seeing-to-reporting, and a flash without substance. The four-witness threshold thus disciplines conversion of an appearance into a report rather than treating multiplied eyesight as automatically reliable.

activation_trace.role: Witnessed presence anchors the changed reading in direct observation.
A water-like mirage supplies a visible appearance that fails under approach.
Supposition supplies the mistaken judgment that converts appearance into expected fact.
Arrival at the apparent object tests whether what seemed present has substance.
Finding replaces visual expectation with discovered absence and then divine presence.
Presence at the thing mirrors the focus's location of final classification at God.
Eye-seeing in layered darkness supplies the perceptual limit.
The split root's report-transmission image exposes the conversion step from seeing to narrated claim.
A false flash without fulfillment supplies the failure mode of brilliant appearance lacking proof.

structural_cues: 24:35-43 alternates light, mirage, layered darkness, seeing, and lightning.
24:39 repeats coming and being at God in a sequence where apparent evidence collapses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies optical failure modes and a mirrored coming/at-God sequence; I infer that they model risks in converting sight into testimony. A live alternative is that these images concern deeds and unbelief independently of the accusation passage.

changed_reading.before: Four observers guarantee truth by sheer number.
changed_reading.after: The threshold is a reliability protocol for converting appearance into accountable report: mirage, darkness, and false flash show why seeing must be stable, direct, and mutually corroborated.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later speech is tested by whether its speakers appear for judgment and embody what they say: some claim belief then turn away, come only when truth favors them, or intensify oaths, while recognizable obedience is the demanded performance. Failure to bring witnesses is therefore a failed speech-act, not merely absent paperwork.

activation_trace.role: A charge that fails to carry through supplies the performative dimension of liar-status.
Uttered profession supplies a claim whose truth is tested by what follows.
Turning away supplies action that defeats the preceding verbal profession.
Judgment between parties supplies the forum at which speech must become accountable.
Coming to judgment only when favored makes arrival itself evidence of selective commitment.
Submission supplies the action that accompanies convenient arrival.
Distributed oath-taking supplies verbal intensity that the passage declines to treat as sufficient.
Recognizable good supplies the plain enacted alternative to emphatic oath performance.

structural_cues: 24:47-51 repeatedly contrasts saying with turning away, appearing for judgment, hearing, and obeying.
24:53 rejects strenuous oath display in favor of recognizable obedience.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies speech/action contrasts and selective arrival at judgment; I infer that the focus's non-arrival of witnesses makes the accusation fail as a performed claim. A live alternative is that later hypocrisy language should not determine the legal semantics of the earlier accusers.

changed_reading.before: A lie is only a false sentence, and absent witnesses are missing paperwork.
changed_reading.after: Liar-status is also performative: accusatory speech that will not arrive at judgment with accountable support fails its own claim, while oath intensity cannot replace evidence or recognizable action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah distinguishes the community's enforceable speech-status from God's complete disclosure of actuality. Unsupported accusers are normatively liars before God now, while full truth, return, information, and recompense remain the divine audit.

activation_trace.role: Presence at God's criterion anchors the focus's present normative classification.
Attribution to lying identifies the enforceable status attached to unsupported accusation.
Completion without deficiency reserves fully rendered consequence for God.
Truth matching reality supplies the complete standard beyond human access.
Full disclosure to the knower distinguishes divine knowledge from communal inference.
Return supplies the transition to final audit.
The report that arrives and is delivered supplies God's final informing of what occurred.
Intentional deeds, not social rumor, are the object of final disclosure.

structural_cues: 24:25 places complete truthful recompense with God.
24:64 closes with God knowing their state and later informing them of their deeds.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a present divine classification and a later complete divine audit; I infer that humans enforce the proof threshold without claiming exhaustive knowledge of the unseen event. A live alternative is that "at God" already states the event's full metaphysical falsity, not merely a normative accuser-status.

changed_reading.before: Failure to prove licenses humans to claim exhaustive knowledge of the unseen event.
changed_reading.after: The focus authorizes a stringent liar-status for unsupported public accusers under God's standard, while complete factual disclosure remains God's audit; the community enforces the threshold without borrowing omniscience.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it maps animal locomotion into evidentiary architecture. It remains anchored because the focus's four-root carries four-force and shared-load images, while 24:45 couples literal fourfold support with roots whose inventories include crawling and walking gossip. Render only as a material analogy, never as the lexical or legal definition of four witnesses.

activation_trace.role: Four twisted forces make the witness body a possible load-bearing support image.
Knowledge-bearing testimony keeps the analogy attached to evidence rather than free metaphor.
Crawling gossip supplies one covert mode by which unsupported speech circulates.
Walking gossip supplies a second social circulation mode.
Literal movement on four supplies the contextual support structure that activates the focus's count.

changed_reading.before: Unsupported rumor can keep moving socially despite lacking proof.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, rumor may crawl or walk, but an accusation is not allowed to stand in the focus until it has four load-bearing witness supports.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the liar-root's deceptive-garment branch through the surah's clothing, adornment, plating, and acquittal images. It remains anchored in "the liars" and in the accusation's effect on public appearance. Render as an image of reputational overlay, not as an alternative dictionary gloss for the verse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The liar designation after failure to bring witnesses.

activation_trace.role: A garment that misreports its own state supplies the image of false appearance attached to a person.
Managed display of appearance supplies the social surface on which reputation is read.
Metal plated to look like precious material supplies a second deceptive-surface mechanism.
A patterned or variegated garment reinforces the image of a constructed visible condition.
Separation and acquittal detach the protected persons from the sayings overlaid on them.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, unsupported accusation acts like a deceptive social garment or plating: it colors the accused's public appearance until witness failure and acquittal detach the saying from the person.

strongest_changes: The ayah became a chain-of-custody gate that converts direct observation, not heard speech, into a public charge.
The nearby spouse sequence distinguished ordinary four-person corroboration from exceptional fourfold self-attestation sealed by a fifth sanction.
Privacy, controlled sight, embodied testimony, and optical failure made the threshold protective and anti-illusion rather than merely numerical.
The liar designation became an accountable and performative speech-status located at God's criterion, while complete factual audit remains divine.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah repetition linked the exact legal formula to rumor flow, guarded interiors, disciplined sight, bodily witness, mirage, and later speech-action tests. The split seeing/reporting root and the four-support branches preserved distinct exploratory models that a single legal paraphrase would lose.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the four-strand and four-legged support analogies are rhetorically active or only lexical-material resonances.
Whether "at God" primarily marks a present normative classification, final metaphysical judgment, or both.
How tightly the privacy and light clusters are designed cross-references rather than coherent whole-surah analogies.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Evidence must arrive through the proper access, not merely be asserted.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ج ي ء` B004 is bringing or presenting something; `ء ت ي` B003 is approaching a matter through its proper way; `ش ه د` B002 is testimony from knowledge and B008 a witnessing sign; `ع ن د` B004 is presence or nearness in judgment. **Structural cue:** the first clause demands that four witnesses be presented, then the second changes the verb and declares the unsupported speakers liars “at God”; 24:12's favorable presumption and 24:15's speech without knowledge frame this demand. **Assigned role:** the witnesses are not decorative corroboration but the authorized access by which an allegation can enter judgment. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies arrival/presentation, proper approach, and decisive classification after non-arrival; I infer valid evidentiary access → admissible claim, while absence of that access → claim classified as false for judgment. **Reading change:** the four-witness rule becomes a route constraint on knowledge, not just a numerical hurdle.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:15 supplied the strongest later correction: “proper access” cannot mean confident delivery, because a report can arrive fluently by tongues and mouths while carrying no knowledge.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A norm becomes effective by being bounded, placed, counted, witnessed, and finally registered at its proper moral magnitude.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Lexical branches make legislation spatial and corporeal: a surah resembles an enclosing wall, obligation a scored cut, punishment a measured impact on skin, and culpability an allocated share whose apparent and actual sizes diverge.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Ordinary Witness Threshold
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A charge crosses into adjudicable knowledge only when a fixed number of present observers can articulate it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: presence with direct observation `quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`; testimony that declares known fact `quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`; the witness as an articulating tongue `quranic:root_000822:B005/m01`; the number four `quranic:root_000536:B001/m01`; bounded individual unit `quranic:root_001631:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Presence, knowledge, articulation, and count cooperate as a single evidentiary gate. A claim does not become proof merely by circulation; four embodied positions must convert observation into public declaration.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P1 24:1-20] Cognition Can Align or Invert a Report
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Before speech becomes public judgment, the mind estimates, orients, and either aligns a report with evidence or turns it away from truth.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The branches distinguish several epistemic operations concealed by broad labels such as “thinking”: strong inference, weak imagining, accusation, habitual suspicion, internal speech, and directional inversion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Falsehood as Directional Inversion
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A statement is turned off its proper heading, stabilized as a lie, and then used to classify other speakers as liars.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: turning something away from its face or direction `quranic:root_000041:B001/m01`; lie diverted from truth `quranic:root_000041:B002/m01`; judgment weakened and deprived of sound strategy `quranic:root_000041:B006/m01`; falsehood opposed to truth `quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`; assigning falsehood to another `quranic:root_001290:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: `إفك` is not only incorrect content; it is an orientation reversed. Once the report is turned, cognition loses strategic soundness and social actors begin projecting the false classification onto others. The channel makes moral error a directional operation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Sexual accusation reaches beyond an isolated act into pairing, marital legitimacy, conception, gestation, birth, and the traces by which lineage becomes socially visible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Womb, postpartum blood, afterbirth, birth witness, midwife, and rapid conception branches disclose the lineage stakes that make sexual testimony unusually consequential.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Gestation and Birth Leave Evidence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A womb receives conception, carries a child, releases birth material, and is attended by recognizable traces and a receiving agent.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: womb as the child's growing enclosure `quranic:root_000552:B003/m01`; pregnancy and postpartum emergence `quranic:root_001533:B005/m01`; blood or membrane accompanying birth as a witness `quranic:root_000822:B006/m01`; afterbirth and uterine discharge `quranic:root_000994:B009/m01`; midwife receiving the newborn `quranic:root_001198:B007/m01`; rapid conception `quranic:root_001372:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The branch network assembles a complete reproductive sequence from roots otherwise active in mercy, selfhood, witness, punishment, reception, and verbal relay. This scene usefully reframes why proof rules guard lineage: birth itself yields bodily witnesses, while rumor tries to manufacture social evidence without them.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi dört sayısını, kırk sayısını, bir topluluğu dört kişiye çıkarma eylemini ve o topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olmayı birlikte doğrular. Geçici çerçeve bu sayısal çekirdeği ve sıra bildiren genişlemeyi doğru biçimde temsil eder.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dörtte bir pay, dört kollu örgü ve dört sayısına bağlı dönemsel nöbetler bu dalın yalın sayısal anlamına katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın sayı biçimleri ile bir topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olmayı bildiren kalıp ayrı tutulur; kalıbın eylem anlamı sayı adlarının tümüne yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Dört sayısını ve bu sayının sıra bildiren kullanımını anlatır; ayrıca bir topluluğu dört kişiye çıkarma ya da topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olma eylemini kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel içerik dört sayısı ve onun sayı dizgesindeki biçimleridir.
Bir topluluğu dört kişiye çıkarma ve o toplulukta dördüncü olma, sayısal çekirdeğin eylemsel genişlemesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar dört ve kırk sayılarını, dörder dağıtım biçimini ve bir topluluğun dördüncüsü olma eylemini aynı sayısal eksende toplar. Hedef dilde adların dilbilgisel cinsiyetine göre ayrı dört biçimleri bulunmadığından iki kaynak biçimi aynı sözcükle karşılanır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dört sayısı ile bir grubun dördüncü üyesi olma anlamının birlikte belirtilmesi gereken genel açıklamalarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dört sayısını ve dördüncü sıraya katılma ilişkisini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Salt sayı, sayma veya kırk gibi onluk bir sayı biçimi söz konusu olduğunda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Yalın sayısal çekirdeği eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir topluluğa katılarak onun dördüncü üyesi olmayı anlatan eylem bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olma ilişkisini korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi bir bütünün dört eşit parçasından birini, malların dörtte birini alma eylemini ve önderin savaşta ele geçirilen mallardan aldığı dörtte bir payı açıkça bir arada verir. Geçici çerçeve bu pay ve alma ilişkisini doğru sınırlar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dörtte bir payı adlandıran yalın biçimler ile bir topluluğun mallarından bu payı alma kalıbı ayrı tutulur; alma eylemi her kullanımda varsayılmaz.

Bir topluluğun mallarından dörtte birini alma, pay kavramının eylemli kullanımını oluşturur.
Önderin savaşta ele geçirilen mallardan aldığı dörtte bir pay tarihsel ve kurumsal bir özelleşmedir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar dörtte bir parça ile bu parçanın alınmasını ortak çekirdek olarak sunar; önderin ele geçirilen mallardan aldığı pay, genel kesir anlamının tarihsel olarak belirlenmiş bir uygulamasıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi iki ayrı gerçekleştirmeyi doğrular: ip ya da telin dört koldan bükülmesi ve bir şeyin kare biçimine getirilmesi. Geçici çerçeve ikisini birlikte anmakta haklıdır, ancak kareleştirme dört kollu bükmenin sonucu gibi okunmamalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dört koldan bükme kalıp içindeki nesnelerle sınırlıdır; kareleştirme biçimi bu kalıptan ayrı tutulur ve kökün yalın anlamı diye genellenmez.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı ayıran özellik dört kol sayısıdır; komşu dalda belirleyici olan sağlamlık ve iki katlı yapıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Verilen bütün ip, tel, büküm, şerit, kol ve kardeş dal adayları değerlendirildi. Sağlam büküm adayı işlem ortaklığını ve dört kol sınırını en açık gösterdi; diğerleri malzeme ya da uzak sayısal çağrışım düzeyinde kaldı.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi deve sulama düzeni ile belli aralıkla yinelenen ateş nöbetini dört sayısına bağlı tek bir dönemsel alanda toplar. Bununla birlikte kaynaklarda günün başlangıçtan mı yoksa aradaki susuz günlerden sonra mı sayıldığı konusunda farklı anlatımlar bulunduğundan kesin gün numarası yerine döngü esas alınmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal mevsimi veya salt dört sayısını değil, dört sayısına göre düzenlenen sulama ve hastalık nöbetlerini anlatır; gün numarası sayım yöntemine göre değişebilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Nöbet adı ile develerin bu nöbette sulanması ve ateşin bu düzende gelmesi kalıpları ayrıdır; dönemsel anlam yalın sayı kullanımına taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Develerin suya götürülmesini veya ateşli hastalığın yeniden gelmesini dört sayısına göre düzenleyen dönemsel bir nöbettir. Kaynakların gün sayma yöntemi değişse de belirleyici unsur aralıklı geri dönüştür.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, dört sayısına göre kurulan ve aralıklarla geri dönen nöbettir.
Develerin belirli günler susuz bırakıldıktan sonra suya götürülmesi bu nöbetin hayvancılık uygulamasıdır.
Bir gün gelip iki gün ara veren ya da dört günlük hesaba göre dönen ateş, hastalık uygulamasıdır.
Nöbetin dördüncü mü yoksa dört günlük bekleyişten sonraki beşinci gün mü gerçekleştiği, başlangıç gününün sayılmasına göre farklı aktarılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar deve sulaması ile yinelenen ateşi dört sayılı bir nöbet düzeninde birleştirir. Sulama gününün dördüncü ya da beşinci diye belirtilmesi özde ayrı bir döngü değil, başlangıç gününün hesaba katılmasındaki farktır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sulama veya ateşli hastalık bağlamından bağımsız olarak dalın ortak dönemsel yapısı açıklanırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dört sayısına bağlı aralığı ve yinelenen nöbet yapısını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Develerin birkaç günlük susuzluk aralığından sonra düzenli biçimde suya götürülmesini anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Hayvanları, sulama eylemini ve dört sayısına bağlı döngüyü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ateşli hastalığın aralık vererek dört sayılı bir düzene göre yeniden geldiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Ateş nöbetini, aralıklı gelişi ve sayısal düzeni korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: dört sayısına bağlı sulama ya da ateş nöbeti
ateşin dört sayılı nöbetle yeniden gelmesi

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal sulama döngüsünü dört sayısına bağlar ve ateş nöbetini de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal beş susuz günün ardından altıncı gün sulamayı belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal develerin suya götürülmesini gün sayısına bağlı dönemsel bir düzende anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Hayvancılık uygulaması ortaktır, ancak döngünün sayısı farklıdır; ayrıca ateşli hastalık anlamı yalnız odak dalda bulunur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal ateşi dört sayısıyla belirlenen özel bir aralık düzenine bağlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal ateşin bilinen zamanda gelmesini söyler, fakat aralığı dört sayısıyla sınırlamaz.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: dört günlük ve genel ateş nöbeti
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da ateşli hastalığın belli zamanlarda yeniden gelmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın ayırıcı sınırı dört sayılı döngüdür; komşu dal ise zamanında gelme özelliğini daha genel bırakır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Verilen bütün aralık, sulama, hastalık, gün adı ve kardeş dal adayları değerlendirildi. Altı günlük sulama ile genel ateş nöbeti, dalın iki uygulamasını doğrudan sınırlar; öteki adaylar yalnız zaman alanını paylaşır.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ورد الإبل المسمى الربع وحمى الربع التي تعاود على هذه النوبة
